prediction.text:
Tesla's total gross profit slipped about 1.2% in FY2024, from $17.66 billion to $17.45 billion. Gross margin fell from about 18.2% to about 17.9%, a drop of about 0.39 percentage points. Revenue grew slightly over the same period. Tesla said the automotive gross margin fell from 19.4% to 18.4%. It attributed this mainly to lower average selling prices on its vehicles and the Cybertruck ramp. Lower per-unit costs and higher regulatory credit and FSD (Supervised) revenue partly offset these.
Tesla's FY2023 gross profit was $17.66 billion.
Tesla's FY2024 gross profit was $17.45 billion.
Gross profit fell about 1.2% year over year from FY2023 to FY2024, so profit did decline, but only modestly.
Gross margin in FY2023 was about 18.2%.
Gross margin in FY2024 was about 17.9%.
Gross margin declined by about 0.39 percentage points between FY2023 and FY2024.
Tesla said the gross margin for total automotive decreased from 19.4% to 18.4% in 2024 due to lower average selling price on its vehicles and the Cybertruck ramp. It said these were partially offset by lower average combined cost per unit of its vehicles and increases in regulatory credit and FSD (Supervised) revenue.
Tesla attributed the lower average selling price to overall price reductions and attractive financing options provided in 2024, as well as mix. It also noted a decrease of approximately 22,000 combined Model 3 and Model Y cash deliveries.
Tesla said the lower cost per unit came primarily from lower raw material costs, freight and duties, as well as mix.

caveats: The company-wide gross profit and margin figures cover all of Tesla, not just cars. The 19.4% to 18.4% figures in the filing text are for total automotive.
The decline in total gross profit was small (about 1.2%). Revenue was slightly higher in FY2024 ($97.69 billion vs $96.77 billion).
The passage that begins 'combined cost per unit of our vehicles...' starts mid-sentence. The preceding sentence on the change in automotive cost of sales was not retrieved.
Automotive gross profit dollar amounts appeared only in a worker note, not in a fact record. I did not use them as numeric claims.
